title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented Rhodes study environments, spanning a 24-hour library area, small group rooms, academic-support spaces, and specialized work settings.

cards.title: Middle Ground
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use this library study area when your work runs past normal building hours; bring your Lynx Card and confirm any term-specific access updates.
cards.short_summary: Rhodes identifies Middle Ground as its 24-hour study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Barret Library lists Middle Ground as a 24-hour study space.
cards.access_notes: The library’s official page identifies Middle Ground as 24-hour study space; confirm current campus-card access rules before going.

cards.title: Study Room 120
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use this named group-study room for a focused working session; check with the library for room availability and any reservation or entry requirements.
cards.short_summary: A current Rhodes room listing identifies Barret 120 as a study room.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 120 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. Availability, reservations, and building access are not stated in the room listing; verify before use.

cards.title: Study Room 222
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Make this a meet-up point for shared reading or problem sets, then confirm with library staff whether the room is open or reservable that day.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor library study room documented by Rhodes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 222 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. The listing does not state reservation procedures or public access rules; confirm before use.

cards.title: Study Room 224
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Choose this numbered library room for a contained group work block; ask the Check-Out Desk about availability before moving your materials in.
cards.short_summary: A specifically identified Barret Library group-study option.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 224 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library; the library lists group study rooms among its services. Confirm room availability and any booking rules.

cards.title: Study Room 230
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Set up here for a collaborative assignment or review session, and verify its availability with the library rather than relying on a posted schedule.
cards.short_summary: A named Barret Library study room on the current Rhodes listing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 230 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. The available source does not give booking details, so check with the library before using it.

cards.title: Study Room 308
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Bring a small team and a clear agenda for this designated study room; confirm access and whether a reservation is needed before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A numbered library study room documented in current Rhodes materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 308 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. Confirm room availability, reservation policy, and building access with library staff.

cards.title: Study Room 310
cards.subtitle: Paul Barret, Jr. Library
cards.notes: Use the named room for a collaborative work session, but check its status first; the official listing confirms the room, not a standing booking schedule.
cards.short_summary: A specifically listed study room within Barret Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes’ current faculty room listing labels Barret Library 310 as a study room.
cards.access_notes: Located in Barret Library. No public booking details were verified; contact the library to confirm access before use.

cards.title: Language Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Palmer Hall
cards.notes: Bring language coursework or digital assignments to use large-screen computer stations, charging, printing, and flexible work areas; reserve group space directly.
cards.short_summary: Flexible work space with large-screen computer stations and student-group reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Language Learning Center lists flexible study/work spaces, large-screen computer stations, charging, printing, and reservable student-group space.
cards.access_notes: Student-group and event space is reservable through the Language Center; its page directs students to contact the Center’s RSA.

cards.title: Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Barret Library, Room 122
cards.notes: Bring a draft at any stage for a writing-focused session; students can drop in for an impromptu appointment or sign up through the Writing Center.
cards.short_summary: A Barret Library writing-support space for scheduled or drop-in work.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes states that the Writing Center is in Barret Library Room 122 and that students may drop in or sign up for a session.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Barret Library in Room 122. Drop-in availability is not guaranteed; students may also sign up through the Writing Center.

cards.title: Testing Room
cards.subtitle: Barret Library, Room 303
cards.notes: Students with approved testing accommodations can reserve a distraction-limited carrel, computer, or height-adjustable station for an accommodated exam session.
cards.short_summary: A reservation-based, distraction-limited setting for eligible accommodated testing.
cards.evidence_claim: Rhodes describes Room 303 as a fob-accessible, distraction-limited testing space with 14 carrels, five computers, and two height-adjustable stations for eligible students.
cards.access_notes: Fob access is limited to Rhodes students with approved Student Accessibility Services testing accommodations; reserve a space for each test.
